description: Force-directed graph layout algorithms (Fruchterman-Reingold, ForceAtlas2) ARE N-body simulations with modified force laws. A gravity sim with repulsive short-range forces and attractive edge-spring forces becomes a graph visualization engine.
mathematical_formalization: ForceAtlas2: F_repulsive(i,j) = k_r * m_i * m_j / |r_ij|^2 (Coulomb repulsion).  F_attractive(i,j) = k_a * |r_ij| for (i,j) in E (Hooke spring).  This is gravity with sign-flipped short-range + edge-only long-range.
implementation_hypothesis: Modify compute_forces() to accept a force_law parameter. Add 'repulsive_gravity' and 'spring_attraction' laws. Feed an adjacency list. Reuse the entire simulation loop. ~40 lines of glue code.
experiment_seed: Load a small social network (Zachary's karate club, 34 nodes) and lay it out using the gravity sim engine with repulsive + spring forces. Compare layout quality with NetworkX's spring_layout.
